text:
Alex R: Heads up — noticed a small latency regression on the canary after the kernel switch, looks correlated with short prompts (<=32 tokens).
Priya S: which kernel flip? the new fused-attn path?
Alex R: yeah, fused-attn-v3. p50 fine but p95 +18ms for short requests.
Mike H: can you paste the quick perf dump?
Alex R: copied from perf-bench run on canary: 
```
model: redwood-v1-small
config: fused-attn-v3, batcher=continuous
traffic: 10k reqs, 60% <=32 tokens
latency: p50=28ms p90=46ms p95=62ms p99=120ms
baseline (v2): p50=27ms p90=44ms p95=44ms p99=110ms
```
Priya S: wow p95 jumped a lot, but p50/p90 small. suggests a tail interaction in batching or KV path.
Emily Z: could be KV cache prefetch or slower kernel for tiny seqs when combined in mixed-length batches. did you check batch-formation histogram?
Alex R: yep. continuous batcher grouped many tiny prompts with a few long ones. batch sizes ok, but decode-rate heterogeneity high.
Mike H: my theory: kernel selection picks fused-attn due to avg seq len threshold, but throughput loss when a long request appears in batch causes token-budget overshoot + queuing at tail.
Priya S: can we try stricter segregation by decode-rate instead of just avg length? e.g., split if stddev tokens > X or if decode-pps differ >Y.
Alex R: tried a quick config tweak on canary: 
```json
{"segmentation": [{"name":"short-low-pps","max_tokens":32,"decode_rate_threshold":200},{"name":"long-high-pps","min_tokens":33}], "token_budget_target_ms": 12}
```
ops-bot: deployed segmentation config to canary (rev d4f2) :rocket:
perf-bot: running synthetic sweep (2k reqs per cohort)
perf-bot: results: short-low-pps p95=48ms (improved from 62ms), long-high-pps p95=70ms (unchanged)
Mike H: good improvement for short cohort. suggests the kernel's per-request overhead was amplified by mixed batches.
Emily Z: what about KV cache hits? did the short cohort see more KV fetching due to evictions?
Alex R: looked at KV hit rate — unchanged overall, but short cohort had slightly lower local KV hit (0.92 -> 0.88) during the canary window when long requests spiked.
Priya S: next actions: 1) replicate with production trace slice, 2) tune token_budget_target lower for short cohort, 3) consider forcing alternative kernel for mixed batches.
Alex R: agreed. I'll run production-trace replay tonight and post results.
Mike H: if replay confirms, we should avoid global kernel flip until segmentation + token budget changes are in place. revert on canary if regressions persist.
Emily Z: I'll add a quick regression test in the perf suite: randomized mixed-length batches with kernel toggles.
Priya S: nice. ping me when replay finishes, I'll prepare rollout plan (canary -> staged) and SLA notes. :+1:
Alex R: thanks — will update thread with replay numbers (ETA ~4h).
